4. Defendant Nos. 1-5 contested the suit by filing written statement and denied all the allegations made in the plaint. The case of the defendant, in short, is that the plaintiff filed Other Class Suit No. 567 of 1982 in the 1st Court of Munsif, Netrokona against the father of defendant Nos. 1-4 for redemption of mortgage and subsequently, the said suit was renumbered as Other Class Suit No. 65 of 1986 and on 25-9-1986 the said suit was fixed for hearing and the defendants filed hazira with witnesses and the plaintiff did not take any step and, as such, the suit was dismissed for default with costs and the plaintiff without filing any miscellaneous case or miscellaneous appeal against the said order, filed a fresh suit on 7-5-1997 against the defendants. 

 8. Mr Md Golam Mostafa, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioner, submits that the plaintiff earlier filed Other Class Suit No. 567 of 1982 which was subsequently renumbered as Other Class Suit No. 65 of 1986 before the Senior Assistant Judge, Netrokona for redemption of mortgage against the defendants which was dismissed for default with cost and without taking any step, after 10 years, the plaintiff again filed a fresh suit seeking the same relief along with additional reliefs in Other Class Suit No. 42 of 1997 which is against the provisions of law. The learned Advocate points out that as per Order IX, rule 9 of the Code of Civil Procedure, where a suit is wholly or partly dismissed under rule 8 of the Code, the plaintiff shall be precluded from bringing a fresh suit in respect of the same cause of action but he may apply for an order to set the dismissal aside if he can satisfy the Court that there was sufficient cause for his non-appearance, but in the present case the plaintiff without taking any step for setting aside the order dated 25-9-1986, the order of dismissal, filed a fresh suit after 10 years, being Other Class Suit No. 42 of 1997 and the relevant provisions of law were not taken into consideration by the Courts below. The learned Advocate next submits that as per section 95(4) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act 1950, the mortgagor is entitled to file an application for redemption of mortgage before the Sub-Divisional Magistrate but in the present case the mortgagor filed suit before the Civil Court. He points out that Ali Hossain executed safkabala deed on 13-1-71 in favour of Abdul Hamid but no agreement was signed by Abdul Hamid on the same date and the alleged agreement was registered on 14-1-1971. The learned Advocate points out that the reliefs sought in the earlier case are the same as in the present case with only an additional relief of permanent injunction. He submits that when the facts, allegations, pleadings in two suits filed one after another are same, the parties are same, the suit land is same and that on the same pleadings the earlier suit was dismissed, even though ex parte, the second suit on the same pleadings is barred under Order IX, rule 9 of the Code of Civil Procedure. In support of his contention, the learned Advocate has referred a decision as reported in 55 DLR 523. The learned Advocate also submits that the plaintiff cannot file subsequent suit after filing an earlier suit, by adding new prayer and relief and the subsequent suit is barred under Order II, rule 1(3) of the Code of Civil Procedure. In support of his contention, the learned Advocate has referred a decision as reported in 10 BLC 283. He also submits that fresh suit for achieving the same relief by adopting indirect method is not permissible which the opposite parties have tried in the present case. In support of this contention, the learned Advocate has referred a decision as reported in 1982 BLD (AD) 54. 

 12. It also appears from the materials on record that the institution and the dismissal of the first suit was not mentioned in the plaint of the subsequent suit and when it was brought within the knowledge of the Court by the defendants in written statements, the plaintiffs amended the plaint and stated the fact of the institution of the first suit. The non-mentioning of the plaintiff about the earlier suit in the print of the subsequent suit shows the intention of the plaintiff to suppress a material fact. 

 14. For the reasons stated above, I hold that the impugned judgments suffer from severe illegality occasioning failure of justice.
